reason: No live Microsoft Graph token was available in this environment. Findings below are from Microsoft Graph v1.0 documentation, not raw tenant responses. Re-run with a Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared token before treating $orderby or $search as supported.

items.question: $search on /events
items.conclusion: Do not use. List events documents OData query parameters and explicitly forbids $filter on recurrence; $search is not documented on either /events or calendarView. Search, attendee and category matching stay in-process over calendarView.

items.question: $orderby=start/dateTime on calendarView
items.conclusion: Docs only say calendarView supports 'some of the OData query parameters'. Do not rely on $orderby. Sort occurrences in-process by start.dateTime. $top is documented: min 1, max 1000.

items.question: isDefaultCalendar on calendar resource
items.conclusion: v1.0 calendar resource includes isDefaultCalendar (boolean): true if this is the default calendar where new events are created. Whether that flag is relative to the caller's mailbox when listing /me/calendars as a sharee is unconfirmed live — do not treat isDefaultCalendar alone as proof a shared calendar is the owner's primary. Pair it with isTallyingResponses as a second signal; IDs from /me/calendars stay in the caller's namespace.

items.question: Does mailbox FullAccess appear in GET /me/calendars without an accepted calendar share?
items.conclusion: Microsoft docs for GET /me/calendars describe local copies from accepted calendar-sharing invitations, not Exchange mailbox FullAccess. Mailbox FullAccess is a different grant (delegated_access_accounts). Until probed live, list_calendars unions /me/calendars with GET /users/{owner}/calendars for each FullAccess owner. Folder-level mail shares are not used.

items.question: getSchedule address cap
items.conclusion: Maximum 20 entities per getSchedule call (users, DLs, or resources). Time window must be less than 62 days. Error 5006 when a slot contains more than 1000 entries.
